title: Local models of the fibres of a composite
statement: Let $a:U\to X$ and $f:X\to S$ be locally finite type morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $u\in U$, $x=a(u)$, $s=f(x)$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{U_s,u}$ and $C=\mathcal O_{U_x,u}$, using scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and local rings (structure-sheaf stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]). These are Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; the induced map $A\to B$ is local (the inverse image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ is $\mathfrak m_A$), its closed fibre is canonically $B/\mathfrak m_A B\cong C$, and it is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] if $a$ is flat at $u$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Each of the three pointed fibres admits an affine open neighbourhood of its indicated point that is finite type over its ground field, namely $\kappa(s),\kappa(s),\kappa(x)$ respectively [def-weil-residue-field]. The stalks and residue fields on these neighbourhoods identify with the indicated fibre stalks and with $\kappa(x),\kappa(u),\kappa(u)$ respectively, compatibly with the residue-field tower $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$.

proof.text: Mathlib composition and base change make the three fibre structure maps locally of finite type. Mathlib locally Noetherian fibre results give Noetherian stalks, and the affine-open basis gives the required pointed affine neighbourhoods with finite type and quasi-compact structure maps and the stated open-immersion stalk and residue isomorphisms.

Define b by the pullback lift of the composite fibre projection and residue-field projection. The pullback lift equations give the two projection identities, and injectivity of the fibre projection gives the point equality.

Transport the stalk map of b along the point equality. The fibre-stalk quotient theorem gives the three surjective canonical projection stalk maps and their kernels. An explicit first-isomorphism quotient argument gives the closed-fibre ring equivalence and its formula on germs.

The stalk square and kernel identities make the square a pushout. Stability of flat ring maps under pushout applied to the flat stalk map of a proves the transported map φ is flat whenever the stalk map of a is flat.
Residue-field functoriality gives the displayed tower identity after transport across the point equalities.
